messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-routing change, we're seeing a ~10-15% p99 regression on the long-seq workload. Running baseline vs new-kernel on same cluster.

mike: Ugh. Which workload? tail or steady?

anna: tail (seq len 2048+, batch size 1). median is unchanged, p50/p90 stable, p99 jumps. I suspect sampling skew in the harness.

raj: Could be grouping by prompt length. Are we shuffling deterministically? Need seed.

anna: I ran with bench harness v3.2 — it shuffles; seed not pinned. Rerunning with `--seed 42` now.

bench-bot: started job 2026-03-20T16:02Z — `bench run --profile long-seq --seed 42 --kernels election=new` — job id b-4821

lucy: Also check KV cache warmup effects. p99 often driven by first few requests when KV miss rate high.

anna: Good call. Will run warmup=5 and warmup=0 for comparison.

mike: Also run with `--stratify-by len_bucket=[0-128,129-512,513-1024,1025+]` so we can see where the regression lives.

bench-bot: job b-4821 finished. Summary: median delta -1%, p90 +2%, p99 +12%. Attached: /mnt/bench/b-4821/report.json

anna: attaching small diff of tail histogram

anna: ```
bucket    baseline_ms    new_kernel_ms    delta_pct
0-128     12.3           12.1             -1.6
129-512   18.7           19.0             +1.6
513-1024  34.2           34.9             +2.0
1025+     210.5          236.3            +12.4
```

raj: Can you paste the run command + env (QUANT_PROFILE)? different quantization paths could change kernel fallback.

anna: run: `bench run --profile long-seq --seed 42 --warmup 5 --kernels election=new --stratify len` env: QUANT_PROFILE=aq8

dmitry: If quant profile differs we should isolate: run both under same QUANT_PROFILE and also force `--kernel=kernel_v2` vs `--kernel=kernel_v1` to bisect.

lucy: Suggest adding output correctness probes: token-level checksum and a tiny eval set to ensure output quality unchanged.

mike: Agreed. Also add `--capture-latency-by-stage` to separate attention/kv/dispatch overhead.

anna: Plan: 1) pin seed+stratify 2) compare kernel_v1 vs kernel_v2 3) warmup variations 4) attach correctness diffs 5) if regression remains, bisect by commit range with bench-bisect tool.

raj: lgtm. I'll help with bisect scripts. @bench-bot can you queue `bisect --metric p99 --target 10% --range 2026-03-01..2026-03-19` ?

bench-bot: bisect queued id b-4822

anna: Thanks all. Will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
